title: How a blockchain keeps score
hook: You and your friends keep a shared notebook of who owes whom snacks. One day someone secretly rubs out a line. How would you ever know?
card1: A [[blockchain]] is a shared record of every [[transaction]]. Thousands of computers keep the same copy, so no single person can quietly change it.
analogy1: Imagine a class notebook where every student has an exact copy. If one person changes their copy, it no longer matches everyone else's, and the class ignores it.
card2: Transactions are collected into a [[block]]. Each new block is linked to the one before it, like links in a chain. Changing an old block would break every link after it.

walk.title: What happens when you send a coin
walk.f1: You press Send. Your wallet signs the transaction with your [[private-key]] to prove the coins are yours.
walk.f2: The transaction goes out to the network. Computers check that the signature is right and that you really have the coins.
walk.f3: Checked transactions are packed into a new block, which is added to the end of the chain.
walk.f4: Every computer updates its copy. The transaction is now on record for good, and anyone can look it up.

card3: Most blockchains are public. Anyone can see which [[address|addresses]] sent coins to which, and when. Your name isn't written there, but the trail stays forever.

record.prompt: A friend says they have sent you 30 coins. They show you a screenshot that says "Sent!"

trust.label: Trust the screenshot
trust.before: You will treat the screenshot as proof that the coins were sent.
trust.what: No coins ever arrived. The screenshot was edited.
trust.why: A screenshot is just a picture, and anyone can change a picture.
trust.how: The proof is the blockchain itself, not a picture of it. Every real transaction can be looked up with a block explorer website.
trust.realLife: Never accept a screenshot as proof of payment. Check your own wallet or a block explorer.

wait.label: Wait a while and hope
wait.before: You will wait and see if anything happens.
wait.what: Nothing changed. You still don't know if they sent anything.
wait.why: Waiting doesn't give you facts. If the transaction were real, the record would already exist.
wait.how: Most blockchains confirm a transaction within seconds or minutes, and you can check its status right away.

check.label: Check your own wallet for the transaction
check.before: You will open your wallet and look for the incoming transaction.
check.what: There is no incoming transaction. You found out right away, without an argument.
check.why: Your wallet reads the shared record. If it isn't on the blockchain, it didn't happen.
check.how: Wallets and block explorers show every transaction to your address, with the time and amount.
check.realLife: Your wallet or a block explorer shows the truth. Screenshots and promises don't.

q1.prompt: Why is it so hard to change an old transaction on a blockchain?
q1.a: Thousands of computers keep the same copy, and the blocks are linked together
q1.c: It isn't: an admin can delete mistakes
q1.explanation: Every block links to the one before it, and thousands of computers hold copies. Changing the past would mean changing almost all of them at once.

q2.prompt: What can anyone see on a public blockchain?
q2.c: Which addresses sent how much to which, and when
q2.explanation: Most blockchains are public records. They show addresses, amounts and times, so think before you share your address.

q3.prompt: A friend shows a screenshot saying they paid you. What is the real proof?
q3.b: The transaction showing up in your wallet or on a block explorer
q3.explanation: The blockchain is the shared record. If the transaction is there, it happened. If not, it didn't.

misc.passwordProtected: "A strong password protects the blockchain." It isn't a password: it's thousands of matching copies and linked blocks.
misc.adminDeletes: "An admin can delete mistakes." There is no admin. Once a transaction is confirmed, nobody can delete it.
misc.fullyPrivate: "Crypto is completely private." Transactions on most blockchains are public, and the trail stays forever.
misc.namesVisible: "My name and address are on the blockchain." Names aren't stored there, but addresses and amounts are, and they can sometimes be linked to people.
misc.screenshotProof: "A screenshot proves it." Pictures are easy to edit. The proof is on the blockchain.
misc.friendWord: "If a friend says so, it's true." Even honest friends make mistakes. The record shows what really happened.

t1: A [[blockchain]] is a shared record kept by thousands of computers.
t2: Blocks are linked, so the past can't be quietly changed.
t3: Check your wallet or a block explorer. Screenshots are not proof.
talk1: Where else do people keep a shared record that everyone trusts, like a school register or a sports scoreboard?
talk2: Is it good or bad that anyone can see blockchain transactions? Why?
